classification.difficultyReason: Requires coefficient matching, an auxiliary transformation and exact solutions within a shifted radian domain.

content.prompt: Solve the following equations in the domain $0\le x\le2\pi$ by first converting to auxiliary angle form.

answer.worked:
Equating coefficients with $R\cos(x-\alpha)$ gives
$$\begin{align*}R\cos\alpha&=\sqrt{3},\qquad R\sin\alpha=1\\R&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2+1^2}=2\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}.\end{align*}$$
Both coefficients are positive, so $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{6}$.
$$\sqrt{3}\cos x+\sin x=2\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right).$$
The equation becomes
$$\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$$
Since $0\le x\le2\pi$, the shifted domain is $-\frac{\pi}{6}\le x-\frac{\pi}{6}\le\frac{11\pi}{6}$.
$$\begin{align*}x-\frac{\pi}{6}&=-\frac{\pi}{6},\ \frac{\pi}{6},\ \frac{11\pi}{6}\\x&=0,\ \frac{\pi}{3},\ 2\pi.\end{align*}$$

Equating coefficients with $R\cos(x+\alpha)$ gives
$$\begin{align*}R\cos\alpha&=1,\qquad R\sin\alpha=\sqrt{3}\\R&=\sqrt{1^2+(\sqrt{3})^2}=2\\\tan\alpha&=\sqrt{3}.\end{align*}$$
Both matched coefficients are positive, so $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{3}$.
$$\cos x-\sqrt{3}\sin x=2\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right).$$
The equation becomes
$$\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=-\frac12.$$
The shifted domain is $\frac{\pi}{3}\le x+\frac{\pi}{3}\le\frac{7\pi}{3}$.
$$\begin{align*}x+\frac{\pi}{3}&=\frac{2\pi}{3},\ \frac{4\pi}{3}\\x&=\frac{\pi}{3},\ \pi.\end{align*}$$

Equating coefficients with $R\cos(x+\alpha)$ gives
$$\begin{align*}R\cos\alpha&=1,\qquad R\sin\alpha=1\\R&=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}\\\tan\alpha&=1.\end{align*}$$
Both matched coefficients are positive, so $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{4}$.
$$\cos x-\sin x=\sqrt{2}\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right).$$
The equation becomes
$$\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{3/2}}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}2.$$
The shifted domain is $\frac{\pi}{4}\le x+\frac{\pi}{4}\le\frac{9\pi}{4}$.
$$\begin{align*}x+\frac{\pi}{4}&=\frac{11\pi}{6},\ \frac{13\pi}{6}\\x&=\frac{19\pi}{12},\ \frac{23\pi}{12}.\end{align*}$$

Equating coefficients with $R\cos(x-\alpha)$ gives
$$\begin{align*}R\cos\alpha&=1,\qquad R\sin\alpha=1\\R&=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}\\\tan\alpha&=1.\end{align*}$$
Both coefficients are positive, so $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{4}$.
$$\cos x+\sin x=\sqrt{2}\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right).$$
The equation becomes
$$\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.$$
The shifted domain is $-\frac{\pi}{4}\le x-\frac{\pi}{4}\le\frac{7\pi}{4}$.
$$\begin{align*}x-\frac{\pi}{4}&=\frac{3\pi}{4},\ \frac{5\pi}{4}\\x&=\pi,\ \frac{3\pi}{2}.\end{align*}$$

Equating coefficients with $R\sin(x+\alpha)$ gives
$$\begin{align*}R\cos\alpha&=1,\qquad R\sin\alpha=1\\R&=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}\\\tan\alpha&=1.\end{align*}$$
Both coefficients are positive, so $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{4}$.
$$\sin x+\cos x=\sqrt{2}\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right).$$
The equation becomes
$$\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{2}}=\frac12.$$
The shifted domain is $\frac{\pi}{4}\le x+\frac{\pi}{4}\le\frac{9\pi}{4}$.
$$\begin{align*}x+\frac{\pi}{4}&=\frac{5\pi}{6},\ \frac{13\pi}{6}\\x&=\frac{7\pi}{12},\ \frac{23\pi}{12}.\end{align*}$$
